transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-30 08:00 PDT | Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Dir ML Eng - Proxima), Maya (CTO), Ravi (Infra), Elena (Security), Jordan (SRE)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Proxima's exit from their current managed provider and viability of Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Heavy emphasis on parity with their current vLLM/TGI stack and security/compliance (KMS, VPC). They asked for a short 48h eval/parity run and SOC2 docs.

Topics: roadmap/timeline, current infra (vLLM + TGI + Azure), latency vs cost tradeoffs, KV cache and prefix caching, quantization compatibility, model variants and rollbacks, canary/A-B routing, audit logs and SSO.

[00:00] Samira: hey everybody thanks for making time, i'll kick us off — short intro from redwood side, then we'd love to understand where you are in the exit and what success looks like for you
[00:18] Alex: thanks samira. quick intros — maya is CTO, ravi runs infra, elena security. we run customer-facing chat and a fine-tuned summarization pipeline. currently hosted on (uh) managed infra from a big vendor, plus a lot of our inference routed through our vllm + TGI combo on Azure VMs for cost reasons
[00:36] Maya: timeline is tight — board wants an escape plan in Q4, ideally a pilot in september. primary goals are cost predictability, comparable latency, and no regression in quality/evals (rouge/qa pass rates)
[00:50] Diego: got it. quick clarifying q — when you say vllm + TGI, is that the open-source runtime for batching and your homegrown sharding?
[01:06] Alex: yeah we run vllm for local inference, TGI forks for some generation ops, and we have a kube+scaling layer that does pre-warming. we've also done INT8 quant for some models.
[01:20] Priya: fine, and what are your p50/p95 latencies today for the chat flows?
[01:28] Jordan: p50 110-130ms for short prompts, p95 around 420ms during peaks. embeddings are separate; we batch those overnight
[01:40] Maya: also important — we need SSO + SCIM, audit trails, KMS integration for envelope keys. can't have sensitive prompt logging persist beyond 30 days without explicit controls
[01:58] Elena: also SOC2 is must-have for procurement, and our legal needs to see encryption-at-rest + in-transit docs, and HSM/KMS architecture
[02:12] Samira: totally. we'll share our security packet including SOC2, ISO notes, and KMS/HSM integration guide after this call.
[02:22] Alex: great. one of our main concerns is parity with our current evals. we've tuned prompts and few-shot examples extensively. how do you approach eval parity and regression detection?
[02:36] Diego: our approach is twofold: we run side-by-side eval harnesses with identical prompts and temperature/seeding to measure quality metrics (we've seen small differences due to kernel/quantization combos), and we also capture token-level diffs to analyze hallucination changes. typical 48-72h parity run uncovers obvious regressions
[02:52] Alex: okay — can you replicate vllm/TGI quirks? we rely on some TGI-specific stopping behavior and custom logits processors
[03:06] Priya: we can add compatible logits processors in the runtime and map stopping tokens. there are cases where semantics differ when quantizing to INT8; we'll flag those and propose model variants (e.g., float16 variant for critical routes)
[03:22] Maya: what about autoscaling and burst? currently when we run campaigns we need fast burst capacity without degrading latency
[03:32] Diego: Dedicated includes reserved pools plus burst capacity; the routing layer can fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated is saturated. for private customers we support burst policies via on-demand nodes in the VPC or hybrid routing to Redwood-hosted fallback with encryption in transit
[03:50] Ravi: hybrid routing is interesting but raises data residency concerns — will plaintext prompts ever hit third-party infra?
[03:58] Samira: we never send unencrypted sensitive payloads to hosted fallback if you opt into strict data residency. hybrid fallbacks can be enabled with envelope keys so Redwood cannot decrypt customer payloads — we can walk through the KMS flow
[04:12] Elena: please document that flow; legal will want to see exact key handoff and ability to audit decrypts
[04:20] Samira: noted, will include in the security packet.
[04:26] Alex: cost question — our current unit cost varies a lot. can you give a ballpark difference between hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[04:36] Priya: ballpark: hosted is simplest and often best for small to medium consumption. dedicated (reserved capacity) reduces per-token costs for predictable throughput by 30-60% depending on batch efficiency and model. private (customer-managed infra) shifts infra costs to you but gives tightest isolation; Redwood charges a platform fee plus support. we will share a tailored estimate post-eval
[04:58] Jordan: and how do you handle KV cache and prefix reuse? that's a big contributor to cost savings for us
[05:06] Diego: our runtime supports prefix caching across requests and per-customer KV cache. for OpenAI-style chat we've seen 2-4x token cost reduction when prefix reuse is high. the cache is TTL-based and configurable; we can instrument cache hit rates per route in the console
[05:22] Alex: any gotchas when migrating from Azure vllm deployments? like kernel-level differences or operator flags?
[05:30] Priya: yes a few. vLLM's attention implementation and TGI tokenization differences can change output. kernel selection (flash attention variants) and quant backends differ across hardware. we'll do a kernel/profile mapping during the parity run and surface any ops that need prompt tweaks
[05:48] Maya: what about canary rollouts and model pinning? we need to test new variants on a slice of traffic and have automatic fallback in case of regressions
[05:58] Diego: console supports rollout policies, canary percentages, and automated rollback rules based on quality/regression alerts. you can pin routes to model versions and schedule phased rollouts
[06:10] Alex: wonderful. for the parity run do you need sample prompts and a subset of our test harness?
[06:18] Samira: yes please send sample prompt set + eval metrics you care about; diego will set up the harness and share a spreadsheet link for results
[06:26] Alex: we'll share a narrowed prompt set (100-200 prompts) and evaluation rubric. also a performance spreadsheet that includes p50/p95 & token counts
[06:34] Ravi: network topology — if we go private we need to know the VPC peering, NAT, egress controls. also curious about telemetry and tracing hooks
[06:44] Priya: for private we provide an operator bundle and control-plane endpoint in your VPC or a customer-managed control plane. we support VPC peering and private link. tracing hooks via open telemetry and per-request tracing ids are available
[06:54] Elena: encryption-at-rest specifics? where are cached KV and logs stored for hosted?
[07:02] Diego: hosted stores KV and ephemeral logs encrypted with customer-managed keys if you supply an envelope KMS. logs retention is configurable and we can disable retention for specific routes
[07:10] Jordan: what about throughput for embeddings? we do large batched embedding jobs nightly and need throughput guarantees
[07:18] Priya: Dedicated reserved nodes can be tuned for high throughput batch embeddings; we can also run embedding pipelines on dedicated GPU pools. for very large offline jobs we recommend a separate reserved fleet to avoid impacting latency-sensitive routes
[07:30] Maya: procurement and legal — typical contract length for dedicated?
[07:36] Samira: typically annual reserved commitment for Dedicated, but pilots can start with month-to-month for the initial pilot. we have enterprise terms available and can share the SOW template after the eval
[07:48] Alex: great. any limitations around model family compatibility? we use a custom fine-tuned model based on an open LLM — will Redwood accept uploads or must we rehost the model?
[07:58] Diego: you can bring your own model artifacts. our onboarding supports common formats (pytorch state dicts, safetensors) and we handle conversion/optimizations. caveat: some custom kernels or exotic operators may require small code patches; we'll surface those early in the parity run
[08:14] Priya: for fine-tuned checkpoints that rely on custom tokens or adapters, we usually keep an adapter-based approach so we can compile the base model once and apply adapters at runtime
[08:26] Maya: great — our last vendor had slightly different tokenization which caused subtle QA drift; want to avoid repeating that
[08:34] Diego: tokenization mapping is part of the parity checklist. we'll include tokenizer diffs and a simple script you can run locally to compare token counts/IDs
[08:44] Alex: are there specific red flags you've seen in prior migrations?
[08:48] Samira: common red flags: heavy reliance on proprietary logits processors that don't map cleanly, tight coupling to vendor telemetry endpoints, and underestimating cold-start behavior on dedicated fleets
[08:58] Ravi: cold starts have bitten us. how does Redwood handle warm pools?
[09:02] Priya: we support pre-warmed instances and hot-standby caches. warm pool sizing is configurable and integrated with autoscaling rules to maintain p95 SLOs
[09:14] Alex: fine. security again — can you provide sample audit logs and an example of access logs we can ingest into our SIEM?
[09:24] Samira: yes we'll include sample log schema in the security packet and provide an endpoint for log forwarding to your SIEM via syslog or cloud-native connectors
[09:34] Elena: SSO options? we use SAML today and want SCIM for provisioning
[09:38] Diego: SAML + OIDC supported, SCIM provisioning for users and teams. role-based access and route-level ACLs are supported
[09:46] Maya: ok, sounds like a plan. let's recap next steps

Recap / Next steps:
[09:52] Samira: recap — you'll share 100-200 prompt eval set, proxima will provide p50/p95 and sample logs; diego will run a 48-72h parity harness on Redwood hosted + Dedicated config (float16 / int8 variants) using your prompts; samira will send SOC2 and pricing + SOW template; priya will prepare quantization notes and kernel differences. we'll aim to deliver initial parity results within 72h of receiving the prompt set

[10:18] Alex: approved. one last ask — can you surface any specific model variant recommendations for our chat route vs summarization route?
[10:26] Priya: yes — initial suggestion: keep summarization on float16 model for quality, migrate chat to int8 quant where latency cost matters but keep float16 fallback for canary. we'll document expected delta in rouge/qa metrics per prompt set

Close:
[10:40] Samira: great, we'll follow up with links and the harness invite. thanks everyone
[10:46] Maya: thanks all
